newsitem.title: MALTA: Malta Central Bank expects 1997 exports growth.
newsitem.headline: Malta Central Bank expects 1997 exports growth.

text.p: The Maltese economy can expect some slowdown in domestic demand this year but this will be partly compensated by an improved performance in the export sector, Malta Central Bank Governor said on Monday.

Francis Vassallo, introducing the Central Bank's 1996 annual report published on Monday, said the Maltese economy grew by 4.0 percent in real terms last year from 5.0 percent the previous year due to slackening in domestic and foreign demand.

The drop in domestic demand was fuelled by lower growth in construction and service activities while fewer tourist arrivals were mostly to blame for lower foreign demand, along with a decline in exports of manufactured goods, the report said.
As a result of weaker demand and lower imported inflation, retail price inflation eased markedly in 1996, reaching 2.94 percent.
The Maltese pound lost ground against the dollar, sterling and the Italian Lira in 1996, but appreciated against the mark and the yen, it added.

The government's deficit continued to widen during 1996 due to an increase in expenditure and a drop in ordinary revenue. As a proportion of nominal GDP the fiscal deficit reached 9.1 percent against 3.1 percent in 1995.

Domestic credit remained the principal determinant of monetary expansion, rising by 19.4 per cent during the year. Although net credit to government accelerated, the overall rate of credit growth slowed down towards the end of the 1996.

The bank said it had maintained a relatively tight monetary policy stance, using reverse repos to absorb liquidity from the rest of the banking system almost throughout the year. As a result, money market interest rates rose marginally during the year.
The Central Bank registered a net profit of 22 million pounds last year, from 25 million pounds in 1995. ($1= 0.38 maltese pounds)
